independent_focused_validation.decision: All four Major findings and the one Minor finding are established in the acquired Springer version of record. The report is correctly scoped and requires no scientific correction.

checks.derivation: Definition3.1 and Theorem3.3 admit arbitrary infinite S, requiring only the target triple. With f=|x|, alpha=beta=1, eta=0, a uniformly one-step solver returning epsilon, S={(0,0,2n)}, h=k and phi(n)=(0,0,2n), every ordering and solver premise holds without ties. Target1/4 from epsilon0=1 with r=1/2 requires K=2, but the target sublevel contains one triple. Its first visit allows only one restart and returns1/2; the second visit returns1/4. Thus actual required work2 exceeds asserted bound1.
checks.assessment: Major false general work guarantee, independent of F2. Concrete complete-fiber grids meet the proposed structural repair.

checks.claim: F2: wrong-radius work is not bounded
checks.derivation: For D=R, Q=[0,infinity), f=|x|/8 and g=max(-x,0), global sharpness holds with alpha1/8,beta1,eta0. A total solver taking one update and returning min(|x0|,8epsilon) on valid starts, but seven unchanged updates on invalid starts, obeys the literal conditional cost C=1 and accuracy contract. The complete two-fiber, tie-free schedule with priorities k and 2sqrt(2)k visits radii1/4,1/8,2 at target1/16. The first two starts are invalid and cost7 each; the third costs1 and succeeds. Actual15 exceeds sublevel3; replacing7 by N yields2N+1.
checks.assessment: Major missing all-start cost cap. The actual Algorithm2 checks declared cost before calling and contains no truncation. Fixed-iteration implementations may already obey the stronger premise; universal failure is not claimed.

checks.claim: F1/F2 combined repair and surviving grid arithmetic
checks.derivation: With downward-complete fibers and positive integer charges, the q-th restart for a fixed pair occurs at counter Tq=sum of its first q charges. Strict increase of h in k forces these visits in order. At every prefix, each pair's charged work is no more than its number of visits; summing bounds total charges by prefix length, and an all-start cap bounds actual work. A nondecreasing priority order, with arbitrary ties, makes the target prefix lie in its sublevel. The polynomial-grid sum is bounded by2tau times the two convergent p-series.
checks.assessment: The sufficient repaired theorem is supported. The source's explicit tie-breaking discussion supplies counterevidence to treating its non-strict biconditional typo as a separate substantive problem.

checks.claim: F3: query iterate returned by Algorithm6
checks.derivation: With q=x^2/2,g=10|x|,Q=R,nu=Mnu=L0=delta=x0=1 and epsilon8, Proposition4.10 gives N=1. The first positive root is a1=1, tau1=1, v0=1 and query x1=1. Its proximal successor minimizes x+10|x|+(x-1)^2/2 and is y1=0. The line-search test accepts0<=4. The expressly returned x_N=x1 has objective21/2>8, also exceeding Lemma4.9's k=1 bound8. Executing the extra printed loop index does not alter stored x1.
checks.assessment: Major invalid concrete inner-accuracy promise and corresponding Holder-method specialization. Returning the accepted proximal sequence fixes this example; complete restoration for arbitrary initialization remains unverified, as the report states.

checks.claim: F4: fixed QCBP penalty under general rNSP
checks.derivation: For n=m=s=1, A=1/2, rho1/2 and gamma2, the rNSP holds for every real or complex v since gamma|Av|=|v|. With ground truth1, y1/2 and e0, choose positive zeta=1/[4(c3+1)] for any proposed c3. The unique QCBP minimizer is1-2zeta. At z0 the objective gap is-1+2zeta and the fixed residual is1/2-zeta, giving E(0)+eta=-1/4. Distance is positive and beta1, so no positive c1 or c2 can validate the inequality. The actual proposition imposes neither matrix normalization nor underdetermined dimensions.
checks.assessment: Major false application-level sharpness implication. It does not establish failure of any particular Gaussian experiment.

checks.derivation: The cone inequality and rNSP give ||z-x||1<=(1+rho)/(1-rho)(||z||1-||x||1+2sigma)+2gamma sqrt(s)/(1-rho)||A(z-x)||2. Applying rNSP to the largest s coordinates of z-x and bounding its l2 tail by ||z-x||1/sqrt(s) yields A_rho=(1+rho)^2/(1-rho), B=(3+rho)gamma/(1-rho). Applying the resulting l2 bound to z-x and xhat-x gives the claimed repair with lambda=B/A_rho, residual lambda sqrt(s)q, alpha=sqrt(s)/A_rho and eta=4sigma+4lambda zeta sqrt(s).
checks.assessment: Sufficient conservative repair is verified. It changes the penalty and depends on gamma; searching alpha,beta alone does not provide it automatically.

checks.claim: F5: signed combined error and feasibility
checks.derivation: For D=[-1,1],Q=[0,1],f=x and g=x^2-x on x<0, zero otherwise, E=x^2 on negative x and x on nonnegative x. Thus |x|^2<=E throughout D and all residual/domain assumptions hold. The uniformly one-step solver returning -min(sqrt(epsilon),1) satisfies the combined guarantee. For epsilon<=1 its residual is sqrt(epsilon)+epsilon, with unbounded ratio to epsilon. Nonnegative objective gap or the stated stronger residual-domination condition would bound feasibility by combined error.
checks.assessment: Minor local quantitative interpretation defect; the formal combined-error theorem and qualitative eta0 feasibility survive.
